# Package publishing

## Scope

Applies when the change touches a package or formula published to a public registry. Not when the package is only consumed, which `aidd-team:dependency-upgrade` covers, or stays in a private registry. Neighbours: `aidd-team:ci-pipeline`, `aidd-team:release-rollout`, `aidd-team:api-design`, `aidd-team:dependency-upgrade`.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-11 | CRA reporting applies to a manufacturer (Art. 14), for a package placed on the market earlier too (`aidd-team:incident-response`). | S10 |
| 2026-12-09 | Beside the CRA, the EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853: software placed on the market after this date is a product, and a missing update can make it defective. | S10 |
| 2027-12-11 | The CRA's main obligations apply. A steward keeps a documented cybersecurity policy, and reports actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents (Art. 24). | S9 |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | The release workflow is a CI/CD protected path (major, the security pool). A first publish names the package, the namespace, and the owner accounts in the Spec, and every owner account has phishing-resistant 2FA. | S1, S6 |
| Specify | The version bump follows the public API diff, not the commit messages alone; a major bump names its migration note. | S3 |
| Specify | The registry's own rules are Acceptance: Maven Central's sources and javadoc jars, `.asc` signatures, and POM metadata; Homebrew's stable tagged release built from source. | S4, S5 |
| Implement | Publish only from CI by trusted publishing (OIDC). The publish job alone gets the OIDC token, as `id-token: write` on GitHub Actions or `id_tokens:` on GitLab CI, and no registry token sits in secrets. Disable token publishing where the registry allows it. | S1 |
| Implement | Provenance goes out with the artifact: npm provenance, PyPI attestations (PEP 740), or a GitHub artifact attestation, built from a public repository. | S2 |
| Implement | A LICENSE matching the manifest's SPDX identifier, a SECURITY.md with contacts, and a contribution guide (OSPS Baseline level 1). Under the CRA, SECURITY.md is the steward's or the manufacturer's vulnerability policy. | S6, S9, S10 |
| Implement | Governance: GOVERNANCE.md names the maintainers, their roles, and how decisions and releases are made; CODEOWNERS asks an owner to review release and security paths; each commit carries a DCO sign-off where the project takes outside contributions. | S6, S8 |
| Review | The dry run's file list holds no secret, fixture, or build leftover, and the API report's diff matches the bump. | S3, S6 |
| Review | Scorecard shows no drop since the last release in Token-Permissions, Pinned-Dependencies, Signed-Releases, Branch-Protection, or Security-Policy. | S7 |
| Roll out | Publish from the tag, with an SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX) beside the artifact. Verify the published artifact's provenance from the registry, and keep the previous version installable. A bad release is deprecated or yanked, never overwritten. | S1, S2, S10 |
| Roll out | Turn on immutable releases and staged publishing where the release host and the registry offer them. A product sold under the CRA states its support period. | S1, S10 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Publish dry run | the package builds, carries its license, and holds no secret or stray file | `npm publish --dry-run`; `uv build` then `uvx twine==7.0.0 check --strict dist/*`; `cargo publish --dry-run`; `gem build`; `dotnet pack` | S6 |
| Public API diff | the version bump matches the change to the public API | the team's api-diff-tool: `cargo semver-checks` at the pin of `rust/cargo-semver-checks`; `npx @microsoft/api-extractor@7.59.3 run` against the committed report; japicmp-maven-plugin 0.23.1 breaking the build on a binary-incompatible change | S3 |
| Publish without a stored token | the publish job signs in by OIDC and no registry token exists | a check of the release workflow. The OIDC token is on the publish job only (`id-token: write` on GitHub Actions). No `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_API_TOKEN`, `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NUGET_API_KEY`, or `GEM_HOST_API_KEY` exists, and the CI's secret list (`gh secret list` on GitHub) shows none | S1 |
| Provenance verification | the released artifact verifies against this repository and workflow | npm's signature and provenance check on a fresh install (references/registries.md); `uvx pypi-attestations==0.0.30 verify pypi --repository <repo-url> pypi:<file>`; `gh attestation verify <file> --repo <owner>/<repo>` | S2 |
| Maven Central bundle check | each jar has its sources and javadoc jars, `.asc`, and checksums, and the POM has name, description, url, licenses, developers, and scm | a script over the staged bundle before upload | S4 |
| Homebrew audit | the formula meets homebrew/core's rules and its test passes | `brew audit --strict --new --online <formula>`, `brew install --build-from-source <formula>`, `brew test <formula>` | S5 |
| Scorecard run | the repository's supply-chain checks hold at release | `scorecard --repo=<repo>` (v5.5.0) or the SHA-pinned scorecard action, failing on a drop in a check the Review row names | S7 |
| Project policy files check | LICENSE, SECURITY.md with a contact, and a contribution guide exist, and the manifest's SPDX license matches LICENSE; GOVERNANCE.md and CODEOWNERS exist, and each commit is signed off where the project uses the DCO | a script over the repository and the manifest (`license` in package.json, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, or the POM) | S6, S9, S8 |

## Owned elsewhere

- How CI builds and signs the artifact (the SLSA build track), and the release pipeline's permissions: `aidd-team:ci-pipeline`.
- The notification clocks for a reported vulnerability, the CRA's among them: `aidd-team:incident-response`.
- Vetting the packages a project consumes: `aidd-team:dependency-upgrade`.

- [references/open-choices.md](references/open-choices.md): its open choices, with aidd's defaults.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
